newsitem.title: USA: Final budget deal reached, Sen. Lott says.
newsitem.headline: Final budget deal reached, Sen. Lott says.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott told the Senate Thursday evening he believes a final budget agreement has been reached.
"I think we have reached a final agreement on a package to go to the Budget Committee," the Mississippi Republican said.
Lott was briefed by Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici, who had spent several hours in meetings with top White House officials and other Republican congressional leaders.
Senior Clinton administration officials said earlier Thursday they were very close to an agreement on a plan to balance the federal budget in five years and give many Americans a tax cut.
Lott told reporters later a balanced budget agreement has been reached with the White House and will be brought for a vote in the Senate Budget Committee Monday.

"Yes, we have an agreement. It's over," he said. The plan calls for balanced budget by the year 2002. It provides for a net $85 billion tax cut over five years including President Clinton's $35 billion five-year tax credit for education.
